source_title: DDOT Oversize and Overweight Vehicles — Frequently Asked Questions
verify_reasons: DDOT publishes no formal superload class; the 120,000 lbs / dimensional thresholds below are the police-escort triggers, used here as the review flag.
The DDOT FAQ specifies police-escort thresholds but no private pilot-car counts and no published night/weekend curfew — routes and times are set per-permit by DDOT.
Legal gross weight limit (80,000 lbs) is a statutory default; the FAQ codifies only single-axle 21,000 and tandem 34,000 (Ch. 25, Title 18 DCMR).

superload_thresholds.note: DC has no formal superload category. Police escort + route confirmation are required at/over 12' wide, 13'6" high, 75' total length, or 120,000 lbs gross (or any Class 1 Division 1.1/1.2/1.3 explosives). The 120,000 lbs gross trigger is used here as the heavy-load review flag.

width.note: police escort required for any vehicle/load 12' wide or wider (private pilot count not published)

height.note: police escort required for loads exceeding 13'6" high

length.note: police escort required for any vehicle/load 75' or longer in total length

weight.note: police escort required for total gross weight of 120,000 lbs or more (over_ft here denotes pounds)

single_trip.note: Single haul permit; allow ~1 week for route confirmation by size/weight. A single trip permit is required instead of an annual tag when length over 70', height over 13'6", or width over 8'6".

annual.note: Tractor Trailer tag $85/yr; Truck Crane or Concrete Pump Truck $85/yr; Dump Truck/Cement Mixer/Trash Truck up to 65,000 lbs $1,193/yr. Allow ~2 weeks for an annual permit.

notes: Permit required for: any vehicle over the DC axle/gross limits (21,000 single / 34,000 tandem), wider than 8'6", over 40' long (non-bus), combined length over 55', height over 13'6", or a bus over 60' long / 8'6" wide.
No fixed night/weekend curfew is published in the DDOT FAQ; DDOT confirms a route based on size and weight and may impose per-permit conditions.
